chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

The contracted slave (mukatab) is whipped when he commits adultery, according to the measure of what has been freed from him. So if he slanders a chaste woman, upon him is that he be whipped eighty, whether he is free or a slave.

key_terms.الْمُحْصَنَةَ: A chaste woman, typically married or previously married.
key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبُ: A slave who has contracted with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom in installments.
key_terms.قَذَفَ: To slander or accuse of adultery without proof.

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for a mukatab who commits adultery?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific hadd penalty for a mukatab (contracted slave) committing zina, establishing that his lashes are reduced proportionally to the unpaid portion of his manumission price, reflecting the juristic principle of partial freedom. It further clarifies that for qadhf (slandering a chaste woman), the mukatab receives the full eighty lashes, demonstrating that the penalty for slander is not mitigated by his slave status. This distinction highlights the nuanced application of hadd punishments in Shia fiqh based on the degree of liberty.
